preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (0xBd51b6D98574327734C1621A7283778c5e6Af86e)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) to disable token swapping and liquidity additions. This will stop all automated liquidity provision and token-to-ETH swaps, effectively freezing transaction functionality for regular users while the owner remains unaffected.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TEGPAY contract has an owner-only function setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled that controls whether automated liquidity provision is enabled. The fixed owner address is 0xBd51b6D98574327734C1621A7283778c5e6Af86e. By impersonating this owner, we can disable this functionality, which will stop all automated token-to-ETH swaps and liquidity additions, potentially freezing transaction functionality for regular users while the owner remains unaffected.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank() and call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) to disable the swap and liquify feature.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Define the owner address constant. 2. Use vm.prank(owner) to impersonate the owner. 3. Call TEGPAY(TARGET).setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false). 4. Verify that swapAndLiquifyEnabled() returns false.

attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.startPrank(OWNER) to begin impersonation. 2. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false). 3. Use vm.stopPrank() to end impersonation. 4. Verify the state change.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because vm.prank() didn't properly impersonate the owner address. The contract's onlyOwner modifier checks if owner() == _msgSender(), and _msgSender() returns msg.sender. While vm.prank() should change msg.sender, it might not be working as expected in this context. I should try vm.startPrank() instead.
